description.narrative: Building on the achievements of Phase I, this second phase of the WASH intervention aims to sustain and expand life-saving WASH services to vulnerable populations, particularly IDPs in Khan Younis, the Middle Area, and North Gaza. The implementation is rooted in Oxfam’s multi-sectoral emergency strategy and continues to align with WASH Cluster priorities, UNICEF technical guidance, and SphereStandards. Implementation will be led by Oxfam with support from localized technical actors, ensuring a context-sensitive and community-based approach. Phase II targets key WASH outputs with expanded scope and geographic reach, addressing the protracted displacement crisis and the strain on fragile WASH infrastructure. Under Output 1.1, 80,000 individuals (13,333 HHs or units) will benefit from increased access to safe domestic water. Approximately 6.5 km of water networks and two water wells will be rehabilitated (4 km funded by UNICEF; 2.5 km and two wells through Oxfam co-financing). The intervention includes provision and installation of water pipes and fittings. Water quality surveillance will be strengthened through engagement of technical support to carry out routine testing 20 days/month over six months, allowing for continuous monitoring and corrective actions. For Output 1.2, 14,850 people (2,475 HHs), including PWDs and CWDs, will benefit from improved sanitation. A total of 1,800 shared emergency latrines will be installed withgender-segregated access at the household level. Latrine slabs will be sourced internationally or locally depending on access constraints. Desludging operations will be supported through a hybrid model using desludging trucks, 15 manual desludging kits, PPE, and labor assistance, including the use of animal-drawn transport where vehicle access is limited. Hand hygiene will be reinforced through installation of emergency hand washing stations and regular provision of liquid soap. Under Output 1.3, access to basic water services will be provided to 50,000 individuals (8,333 HHs) through water trucking and installation of water storage infrastructure. This includes 30 bladders supplied by UNICEF and 50 community tanks (1m³ capacity) to be procured based on access feasibility. These efforts aim to maintain safe and reliable water access in informal IDP camps, shelters, and host communities. Under Output 1.4, 31,360 people (5,227 HHs) will receive emergency hygiene kits and essential WASH NFIs, with priority to vulnerable groups such as PWDs and CWDs. Hygiene promotion activities will reach 14,850 individuals through door-to-door awareness sessions, community-led initiatives, training of community mobilizers, and dissemination of context-adapted IEC materials. Mobilizers will receive structured support and incentives to ensure consistent outreach over three months. Under Output 1.5, 15 healthcare facilities; mainly governmental oneswill receive WASH support to benefit 15,000 individuals. This will be coordinated with Health actors and with Health section as required. Activities include repair of water and sanitation systems, distribution of public health IEC materials, training of healthcare personnel on hygiene promotion and water related massages, and community outreach led by trained facilitators working within the facilities for two months. Output 1.6 provides a contingency mechanism to address emerging WASH priorities identified by UNICEF in coordination with the WASH Cluster. These resources will ensure flexible, rapid response to unforeseen needs or scale-up during the project’s lifetime, subject to UNICEF’s prior approval.

participating-org.narrative: The Palestinian Environmental Friends Association is a non-profit organization (Nongovernmental Organization). It was establishmentin 1998 by a group of Palestinian experts to meet the demand needed in the field of the environment and natural resources.The establishment of PEF enables environmental friends all over the world to cooperate neglecting geological and political constrains to stopthe negative impacts on the environment. Together, we create a universal free from pollution, sustainable and suitable for new generations. PEF practiced projects almost all over Gaza Strip. The projects activities mainly covered the following areas: Water and wastewater, public health, global warming, infrastructure and capacity building activities, compost production, solid wastes and awareness programs. The association aim is to share in improving the environmental situation in the Palestinian territories, also, to protect the local environment, and public health natural resources from pollution and mining.
